mcqs.question: "Drugs and poisons" is a subject in which list of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution?
mcqs.explanation: Both Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on drugs and poisons.

mcqs.question: The Drugs Enquiry Committee of 1930–31 was chaired by:
mcqs.explanation: It is called the Chopra Committee after its chairman.

mcqs.question: A Bill becomes an Act after it is passed by both Houses and:
options: is approved by the Supreme Court
is signed by the Prime Minister
mcqs.explanation: Presidential assent turns a passed Bill into an Act.

mcqs.question: Detailed procedures, forms and fees under an Act are usually laid down in the:
mcqs.explanation: Rules are delegated legislation made by the Government under the Act.

mcqs.question: The NDPS Act, 1985 replaced which of the following?
mcqs.explanation: It also replaced the Opium Acts of 1857 and 1878.

mcqs.question: A cognizable offence is one in which:
options: only a fine can be imposed
police can arrest without a warrant
mcqs.explanation: Cognizable means police may arrest and investigate without a warrant.

mcqs.question: Pharmacy Practice Regulations were framed by the PCI in the year:
mcqs.explanation: PCI framed the Pharmacy Practice Regulations in 2015.

mcqs.question: The Drug Price Control Orders are issued under the:
mcqs.explanation: Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act empowers price control.

mcqs.question: The Pharmacy Council of India was constituted in:
mcqs.explanation: The Act was passed in 1948 and the PCI constituted in 1949.

mcqs.question: The term of office of elected and nominated members of the PCI is:
mcqs.explanation: Members hold office for five years.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an ex officio member of the PCI?
options: Director of the Central Drugs Laboratory
President of the Indian Pharmaceutical Association
mcqs.explanation: DGHS, DCGI and Director of CDL are ex officio members.

mcqs.question: The register of pharmacists of a State is maintained by the:
mcqs.explanation: Each State Council keeps the State register; PCI keeps the Central Register.

mcqs.question: Education Regulations under the Pharmacy Act are framed by the:
mcqs.explanation: PCI frames Education Regulations (now ER-2020).

mcqs.question: Under ER-2020, the D.Pharm practical training must be at least:
options: 500 hours over not less than three months
mcqs.explanation: ER-2020 requires at least 500 hours spread over at least three months.

mcqs.question: An appeal against removal of a name from the State register lies to the:
mcqs.explanation: The Act provides an appeal to the State Government.

mcqs.question: A Joint State Pharmacy Council is formed by:
options: an order of the Supreme Court
an agreement between two or more States
mcqs.explanation: States agree to share one council for a fixed period.

mcqs.question: A drug sold under the name of another drug is called:
mcqs.explanation: Imitating or using another drug's name makes it spurious.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is excluded from the definition of cosmetic?
mcqs.explanation: The Act's definition of cosmetic excludes soap.

mcqs.question: The Chairman of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board is the:
mcqs.explanation: DGHS is the ex officio Chairman of DTAB.

mcqs.question: The Drugs Consultative Committee has one representative from each State and:
options: two representatives of the Central Government
mcqs.explanation: DCC secures uniform administration of the Act.

mcqs.question: The appellate drug-testing laboratory under the Act is the:
mcqs.explanation: CDL's report is conclusive when an analyst's report is challenged.

mcqs.question: The import licence for drugs other than those in Schedule X is granted in Form:
mcqs.explanation: Form 10 is for non-X drugs; Form 10A for Schedule X drugs.

mcqs.question: The First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act lists:
options: authoritative books of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani
diseases no drug may claim to cure
mcqs.explanation: The Second Schedule gives standards of quality.

mcqs.question: A drug prepared or stored under insanitary conditions is:
mcqs.explanation: Insanitary preparation is one ground for adulteration.

mcqs.question: Licence to manufacture drugs other than those in Schedules C, C(1) and X is granted in Form:
mcqs.explanation: Form 28 is for C and C(1) drugs.

mcqs.question: Retail sale licence for drugs in Schedules C and C(1) (excluding X) is in Form:
mcqs.explanation: Form 20 is for other drugs; 21 for C and C(1).

mcqs.question: Records of Schedule H1 drugs must be kept for:
mcqs.explanation: The H1 register is kept for three years and open to inspection.

mcqs.question: The label 'Caution: It is dangerous to take this preparation except under medical supervision' is for Schedule:
mcqs.explanation: Schedule G drugs carry this caution.

mcqs.question: Good Manufacturing Practices are laid down in Schedule:
mcqs.explanation: Schedule M covers GMP; Schedule N covers pharmacy equipment.

mcqs.question: A licence for a person who uses another manufacturer's factory to make his products is a:
mcqs.explanation: Loan licences are Form 25A or 28A.

mcqs.question: Schedule X drugs must be dispensed against a prescription written in:
mcqs.explanation: One copy of the Schedule X prescription is retained by the retailer.

mcqs.question: Life period (shelf life) of drugs is given in Schedule:
mcqs.explanation: Schedule P gives shelf life and storage conditions.

mcqs.question: Charas is:
options: the separated resin of the cannabis plant
the juice of the opium poppy
mcqs.explanation: Ganja is the flowering or fruiting tops.

mcqs.question: Under the NDPS Act, possession of a commercial quantity is punishable with rigorous imprisonment of:
options: not less than 10 years, up to 20 years
mcqs.explanation: Commercial quantity also attracts a fine of ₹1–2 lakh.

mcqs.question: The agency that coordinates action against illicit drug traffic in India is the:
mcqs.explanation: NCB coordinates enforcement nationally and internationally.

mcqs.question: Opium poppy cultivation and opium production are supervised by the:
mcqs.explanation: The Central Government controls opium through the Narcotics Commissioner.

mcqs.question: 'Essential narcotic drugs' were introduced in the NDPS Act by the amendment of:
mcqs.explanation: The 2014 amendment aimed at better access to pain relief.

mcqs.question: Acetic anhydride and ephedrine are examples of:
mcqs.explanation: Precursor chemicals used to make narcotics are controlled substances.

mcqs.question: Under the Poisons Act, 1919, the import of poisons is regulated by the:
mcqs.explanation: Possession and sale are regulated by States; import by the Centre.

mcqs.question: Which UN convention of 1971 relates to the NDPS Act?
mcqs.explanation: 1961 was the Single Convention; 1988 the illicit traffic convention.

mcqs.question: A talisman, mantra or kavacha claimed to cure disease is called a:
mcqs.explanation: The DMR Act prohibits advertising magic remedies.

mcqs.question: Which advertisement is exempted under the DMR Act?
options: A newspaper ad of a cure for diabetes
An advertisement sent confidentially to registered medical practitioners
A poster claiming improved sexual capacity
A TV ad of an amulet that cures cancer
mcqs.explanation: Confidential ads only to RMPs are exempted.

mcqs.question: The DMR Act was passed in:
mcqs.explanation: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954.

mcqs.question: Under the DMR Act, advertisements for which purpose are prohibited?
mcqs.explanation: Miscarriage, contraception, sexual capacity, menstrual disorders and Schedule diseases are covered.

mcqs.question: CPCSEA was constituted under the:
options: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
mcqs.explanation: Chapter IV of the PCA Act provides for the committee.

mcqs.question: Each IAEC must include a nominee of the:
mcqs.explanation: CPCSEA main and link nominees sit on every IAEC.

mcqs.question: Using cell cultures instead of animals is an example of:
mcqs.explanation: Replacement means using non-animal methods.

mcqs.question: Under the PCA Act, 'animal' means:
options: any living creature other than a human being
mcqs.explanation: The Act's definition is very wide.

mcqs.question: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority was set up in:
mcqs.explanation: NPPA was set up in 1997 to fix and enforce drug prices.

mcqs.question: Under DPCO 2013 the retailer margin added to the average price to retailer is:
mcqs.explanation: Ceiling price = average PTR × 1.16.

mcqs.question: Scheduled formulations under DPCO 2013 are the medicines in the:
options: Schedule H of the Drugs Rules
mcqs.explanation: DPCO 2013 is based on essentiality.

mcqs.question: For a non-scheduled formulation, the MRP may not be increased in a year by more than:
mcqs.explanation: NPPA monitors increases above 10% in twelve months.

mcqs.question: Ceiling prices are revised every year according to the:
mcqs.explanation: Annual revision follows the WPI of the previous year.

mcqs.question: Only brands with at least how much market share are counted for the ceiling price?
mcqs.explanation: The simple average of PTR of brands with at least 1% share is taken.

mcqs.question: NLEM 2022 contains:
mcqs.explanation: NLEM 2022 lists 384 medicines.

mcqs.question: DPCO 2013 is issued under the:
mcqs.explanation: Price orders are made under section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act.

mcqs.question: Selling drugs by moving from door to door is called:
mcqs.explanation: Hawking of drugs is unethical and must be avoided.

mcqs.question: If a prescription contains an obvious overdose, the pharmacist should:
options: tell the patient the doctor is wrong
mcqs.explanation: Changes need the prescriber's consent.

mcqs.question: Secret commission arrangements between a pharmacist and a doctor are called:
mcqs.explanation: The code forbids clandestine arrangements.

mcqs.question: The principle 'do no harm' is called:
mcqs.explanation: Beneficence is doing good; non-maleficence is avoiding harm.

mcqs.question: Respecting a patient's right to make informed decisions is the principle of:
mcqs.explanation: Autonomy means self-determination.

mcqs.question: Which of these falls under the code of ethics in relation to his trade?
mcqs.explanation: Trade covers price, fair trading, purchase, hawking and advertising.

mcqs.question: Compared with law, ethics generally sets:
mcqs.explanation: Law sets the minimum; ethics expects more.

mcqs.question: Keeping a patient's medicines private from his neighbour reflects:
mcqs.explanation: Patient information must not be disclosed.

mcqs.question: The FSSAI functions under the:
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
mcqs.explanation: FSSAI was set up in 2008 under the Health Ministry.

mcqs.question: Health supplement labels must carry the statement:
options: To be sold on prescription only
mcqs.explanation: Supplements are food, not medicine.

mcqs.question: Under the MTP Act as amended in 2021, termination up to 20 weeks requires the opinion of:
mcqs.explanation: Two RMPs are needed for 20–24 weeks for special categories.

mcqs.question: Termination beyond 24 weeks for substantial foetal abnormalities needs the opinion of a:
mcqs.explanation: The 2021 amendment created Medical Boards in every State/UT.

mcqs.question: For termination of pregnancy of a minor, consent is needed from the:
mcqs.explanation: An adult woman's own consent is sufficient.

mcqs.question: Under the Clinical Establishments Act, registration at district level is done by the:
options: District Registering Authority headed by the District Collector
mcqs.explanation: The District Registering Authority grants provisional and permanent registration.

mcqs.question: The Food Safety and Standards Act replaced the:
mcqs.explanation: It consolidated earlier food laws.

mcqs.question: The Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act was passed in:
mcqs.explanation: Clinical Establishments Act, 2010.

mcqs.question: CDSCO is headed by the:
mcqs.explanation: DCGI is the Central Licensing Authority.

mcqs.question: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission is located at:
mcqs.explanation: IPC is an autonomous body at Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.

mcqs.question: The National Coordination Centre for the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India is the:
mcqs.explanation: IPC runs PvPI as the national coordination centre.

mcqs.question: Medical devices of the highest risk are placed in class:
mcqs.explanation: Class A is low risk; class D high risk.

mcqs.question: The Medical Devices Rules, 2017 came into force on:
mcqs.explanation: MDR 2017 took effect on 1 January 2018.

mcqs.question: Manufacture of class A and B medical devices is licensed by the:
mcqs.explanation: Class C and D are licensed centrally.

mcqs.question: The online portal of CDSCO for import, clinical trial and new drug applications is:
mcqs.explanation: SUGAM handles central regulatory applications.

mcqs.question: A report of corrective actions sent after an inspection is called a:
mcqs.explanation: CAPA = corrective and preventive action.

mcqs.question: Phase I clinical trials are usually conducted on:
options: a small number of healthy volunteers
a large number of patients in many centres
mcqs.explanation: Phase I tests safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics.

mcqs.question: Post-marketing surveillance is:
mcqs.explanation: Phase IV follows approval.

mcqs.question: A BCS Class II drug has:
mcqs.explanation: Its absorption is limited by dissolution.

mcqs.question: The New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 replaced:
options: Schedule Y and Part XA of the Drugs Rules
mcqs.explanation: NDCT Rules now govern new drugs and clinical trials.

mcqs.question: A generic drug is approved in the USA through an:
mcqs.explanation: ANDA needs pharmaceutical equivalence and bioequivalence.

mcqs.question: The term of a patent in India is:
options: 20 years from the date of filing
mcqs.explanation: Patents last 20 years from filing.

mcqs.question: Section 3(d) of the Indian Patents Act prevents:
mcqs.explanation: New forms of known substances need enhanced efficacy.

mcqs.question: Under BCS, a drug is highly soluble if its highest dose dissolves in:
mcqs.explanation: Solubility is tested across the GI pH range at 37 °C.

mcqs.question: Sharps such as needles are collected in a:
mcqs.explanation: White category is for sharps.

mcqs.question: Contaminated recyclable plastics like IV sets and catheters go into the:
mcqs.explanation: Red waste is autoclaved, shredded and recycled.

mcqs.question: The BMW Management Rules, 2016 are made under the:
mcqs.explanation: The prescribed authority is the State Pollution Control Board.

mcqs.question: Untreated bio-medical waste should not be stored for more than:
mcqs.explanation: Waste must be treated within 48 hours.

mcqs.question: Discarded glassware and metallic body implants go into the:
mcqs.explanation: Blue cardboard boxes are used for glass and implants.

mcqs.question: Platelet concentrates are stored at:
mcqs.explanation: Platelets are stored at room temperature with agitation for up to 5 days.

mcqs.question: The minimum haemoglobin for a blood donor is:
mcqs.explanation: Donor Hb must be at least 12.5 g/dL.

mcqs.question: Shelf life of red cells stored in CPDA-1 at 2–6 °C is:
mcqs.explanation: In SAGM additive solution it is 42 days.

mcqs.question: The Nuremberg Code was framed in:
mcqs.explanation: It followed the trial of doctors after the Second World War.

mcqs.question: The Belmont Report gave the principles of respect for persons, beneficence and:
mcqs.explanation: The 1979 Belmont Report set three principles.

mcqs.question: The ICMR National Ethical Guidelines for research on human participants were issued in:
mcqs.explanation: Earlier versions were 2000 and 2006.

mcqs.question: The Declaration of Helsinki was adopted by the:
mcqs.explanation: Adopted in 1964 and revised several times.

mcqs.question: The NDMA is chaired by the:
mcqs.explanation: SDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister.

mcqs.question: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 created the:
mcqs.explanation: CCPA acts on consumer rights violations and misleading ads.

mcqs.question: The District Disaster Management Authority is headed by the:
mcqs.explanation: DDMA plans and coordinates at district level.

mcqs.question: Which is NOT one of the consumer rights under the Consumer Protection Act?
mcqs.explanation: The six rights are safety, information, choice, to be heard, redressal and awareness.
